description: Probability theory and statistics built for computer scientists, with every distribution simulated in R before and after it is derived. Taught to the depth of a full probability course for computer scientists.
modelledOn: Ross, A First Course in Probability
Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Probability
Walpole, Myers, Myers and Ye, Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists
outcomes: Compute probabilities of events with counting, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem.
Work with discrete and continuous random variables, their PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, expectations and variances.
Recognise and apply the standard distributions, including Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson, uniform, exponential and normal.
Use moments and moment generating functions to derive properties and sums of random variables.
Apply the law of large numbers and central limit theorem and construct confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
Simulate random processes in R and use the results to check analytic answers and estimate hard quantities.

units.title: Probability theory
topics: Sample spaces, events, set operations; axioms of probability
Counting: permutations, combinations, multinomials; birthday problem and hash collisions
Conditional probability, multiplication rule, law of total probability
Bayes' theorem: medical tests, spam filters, malaria rapid tests with false positives
Independence and conditional independence; reliability of series and parallel systems

units.title: Random variables
topics: Discrete random variables, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions
Continuous random variables, probability density functions; the CDF as the bridge
Expectation, variance, standard deviation; linearity of expectation
Functions of random variables; expectation of a function
Indicator variables and counting with expectation (expected number of collisions, fixed points)

units.title: Special distributions
topics: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric
Poisson distribution and the Poisson process: arrivals at a bank, packets at a router
Uniform, exponential (memorylessness) and gamma distributions
Normal distribution: standardisation, tables, the 68-95-99.7 rule; normal approximation to binomial
Choosing a distribution for a real situation; fitting and checking in R

units.title: Moments and moment generating functions
topics: Moments about the origin and about the mean; skewness and kurtosis
Moment generating functions: definition, computing moments, uniqueness
MGFs of the standard distributions; sums of independent random variables
Characteristic functions and probability generating functions in brief

units.title: Joint probability distributions
topics: Joint, marginal and conditional distributions for discrete and continuous pairs
Independence of random variables; covariance and correlation
Conditional expectation and the law of iterated expectation
Sums of random variables, convolution; distribution of the maximum and minimum
Bivariate normal distribution; transformations of two variables

units.title: Special probability theorems
topics: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities; Chernoff bounds for randomised algorithms
Weak and strong laws of large numbers
Central limit theorem: statement, intuition and simulation
Applications: Monte Carlo estimation, error in polling, load on a server

units.title: Statistics: estimation and testing
topics: Descriptive statistics, histograms, boxplots, sample mean and variance
Point estimation: method of moments, maximum likelihood; bias and consistency
Confidence intervals for means and proportions; t-distribution
Hypothesis testing: null and alternative, p-values, type I and II errors, z and t tests, chi-square tests
Simple linear regression and correlation; A/B testing a web page

units.title: Computer simulation in R
topics: Pseudo-random numbers; sample, runif, rnorm, rbinom and friends; setting seeds
Simulating games, queues and random walks; estimating probabilities and expectations
Inverse transform and rejection sampling to generate any distribution
Bootstrap confidence intervals; visualising sampling distributions
Project: simulate a mobile-money transaction system or a classroom's exam scores and compare with theory
